title: Homily I — The depth of God's goodness: blessed among women

edition.locus: Migne, PG 96 (Paris, 1860), Homily I on the Dormition, cols. 709-712 (PDF leaves 396-397)

source_text: Ὦ βάθος πλούτου, καὶ σοφίας, καὶ γνώσεως Θεοῦ· κἀγὼ γὰρ εἰς καιρὸν τῷ Ἀποστόλῳ συμφθέγγομαι, ὡς ἀνεξερεύνητα τὰ κρίματα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἀνεξιχνίαστοι αἱ ὁδοὶ αὐτοῦ! Ὦ ἀπλήστου ἀγαθότητος Θεοῦ! ὦ ἀγάπης οὐκ ἐχούσης ἔρευναν! Ὁ καλῶν τὰ μὴ ὄντα ὡς ὄντα, ὁ πληρῶν τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν, οὗ ὁ οὐρανὸς θρόνος, ἡ δὲ γῆ ὑποπόδιον, εὐρύχωρον ἐνδιαίτημα, τὴν γαστέρα τῆς οἰκείας δούλης ἐποιήσατο, καὶ ἐν αὐτῇ τὸ πάντων καινότερον ἀποτελεῖ μυστήριον. Θεὸς γὰρ ὢν, ἄνθρωπος γίνεται, ὑπερφυῶς τε τῷ χρόνῳ τῆς κυήσεως τίκτεται, καὶ διανοίγει μήτραν, τὰ κλεῖθρα τῆς παρθενίας μὴ λυμηνάμενος, καὶ ἀγκάλαις γηΐναις ὡς βρέφος βαστάζεται, τὸ τῆς δόξης ἀπαύγασμα, ὁ χαρακτὴρ τῆς τοῦ Πατρὸς ὑποστάσεως, ᾧ φέρονται τὰ σύμπαντα τῷ ῥήματι τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ. Ὦ θείων ἀληθῶς θαυμάτων! ὦ μυστηρίων τῶν ὑπὲρ φύσιν καὶ ἔννοιαν! ὦ παρθενικῶν αὐχημάτων τῶν ὑπὲρ ἄνθρωπον! τί τοῦτο τὸ μέγα περὶ σὲ, ὦ ἱερὰ μῆτερ καὶ παρθένε, μυστήριον; Εὐλογημένη σὺ ἐν γυναιξὶν, καὶ εὐλογημένος ὁ καρπὸς τῆς κοιλίας σου. Μακαρία εἶ ἐν γενεαῖς γενεῶν, ἡ μόνη ἀξιομακάριστος. Ἰδοὺ γὰρ μακαρίζουσί σε πᾶσαι γενεαὶ, ὥσπερ ἔφησας. Σὲ εἶδον θυγατέρες Ἱερουσαλὴμ, τῆς Ἐκκλησίας λέγω, καὶ ἐμακάρισάν σε αἱ βασίλισσαι, ἤτοι δικαίων ψυχαὶ, καὶ εἰς αἰῶνας αἰνέσουσί σε.
pass_a_gloss: O depth (βάθος) of riches and of wisdom and of knowledge of God; for I too at the right time speak together with the Apostle, how unsearchable his judgments (κρίματα) and untraceable his ways! O insatiable (ἄπληστος) goodness (ἀγαθότης) of God! O love (ἀγάπη) not having searching-out (ἔρευνα)! The one calling the non-existent things as existing, the one filling heaven and earth, whose throne the heaven and the earth footstool (ὑποπόδιον), made the womb (γαστήρ) of his own slave-woman (δούλη) a roomy (εὐρύχωρον) dwelling (ἐνδιαίτημα), and in it accomplishes (ἀποτελεῖ) the newest (καινότερον) mystery of all. For being God, he becomes man, and supernaturally (ὑπερφυῶς) at the time of gestation (κύησις) is born, and opens (διανοίγει) the womb (μήτρα), not having damaged the bars (κλεῖθρα) of virginity, and in earthly arms (ἀγκάλαι) is carried (βαστάζεται) as an infant (βρέφος), the radiance (ἀπαύγασμα) of the glory, the stamp (χαρακτήρ) of the Father's hypostasis (ὑπόστασις), by whom all things are borne (φέρονται) by the word of his mouth. O truly divine wonders (θαύματα)! O mysteries above nature and thought (ἔννοια)! O virginal boasts (αὐχήματα) above man! What is this great mystery about you, O holy mother and virgin? Blessed (εὐλογημένη) you among women, and blessed the fruit of your belly (κοιλία). Happy (μακαρία) you are in generations of generations, the only one worthy to be called happy. For behold all generations call you happy, as you said. The daughters of Jerusalem saw you, of the Church I mean, and the queens (βασίλισσαι) called you happy, that is, souls of righteous ones, and to the ages they will praise (αἰνέσουσι) you.
pass_b_english: “Oh, the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God!” I too, at the right moment, join my voice to the Apostle's: “How unsearchable are his judgments, and how untraceable his ways!” (Romans 11:33). Oh, the boundless goodness of God! Oh, love that cannot be searched out! He who “calls the things that are not as though they were” (Romans 4:17), who “fills heaven and earth” (Jeremiah 23:24), whose throne is heaven and the earth his footstool (Isaiah 66:1), made the womb of his own servant a spacious dwelling, and in it he brings to completion the newest mystery of all. For, being God, he becomes man; at the due time of pregnancy he is born in a way beyond nature; he opens the womb (Luke 2:23) without harming the bolts of virginity; and he is carried as a baby in earthly arms, he who is “the radiance of glory, the exact imprint of the Father's being,” who upholds all things “by the word of his mouth” (Hebrews 1:3).

Oh, wonders truly divine! Oh, mysteries beyond nature and beyond thought! Oh, glories of virginity beyond anything human! What is this great mystery concerning you, holy mother and virgin? “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb” (Luke 1:42). You are blessed from generation to generation, you alone worthy to be called blessed. For see, “all generations call you blessed,” as you said (Luke 1:48). The daughters of Jerusalem (of the Church, I mean) have seen you, and the queens, that is, the souls of the righteous, have called you blessed, and they will praise you for ever (Song of Songs 6:9).

choices.note: Hebrews 1:3 is quoted, not marked in the margin;
John reads 'by the word of his mouth' where Hebrews has 'by the word of his power'.
ὑπόστασις in the Hebrews quotation is rendered 'being' following the Scripture wording.
'He opens the womb' (διανοίγει μήτραν) echoes the firstborn law as quoted in Luke 2:23 (Exodus 13:2); not in the margin, cited as a clear verbal echo.
The margin's Luke 1:28 for 'Blessed are you among women' reflects the received text of 1:28; the full saying with 'fruit of your womb' is Luke 1:42, cited here.
Song of Songs: margin 'Cant. 6:8' (Vulgate numbering), LXX and English 6:9;
John reshapes the verse to address Mary and adds 'daughters of Jerusalem' (a phrase found elsewhere in the Song).
'Blessed from generation to generation' is not cited (no clear single verse).
Edition note (4): R. adds after τῷ Ἀποστόλῳ the words τῆς παρακοῆς ἐδεδίει τὸ ἐπιτίμιον ('feared the penalty of disobedience'), which do not fit; not translated.
Edition note (5): R. has an unclear word printed βυήσομαι after ὑπὲρ φύσιν καὶ ἔννοιαν; not translated.
ἄπληστος ('insatiable') rendered 'boundless', since 'never satisfied' reads as a fault in English.
'And they will praise you' is also from Song 6:9 LXX, so the citation stands after it.
